summary: The run acquired several useful upgrades and reached the Slime Boss, but entered the final stretch with critically low HP after the Gremlin Nob encounter. The main recurring issue was prioritizing setup, card draw, or upgrades while vulnerable instead of securing immediate survivability. The final boss fight then continued that pattern, with defensive options available while at low HP and facing attacks.

lessons.title: Heal before a dangerous elite when already damaged
lessons.situation: At a campfire before an elite or other high-risk fight, especially when HP is no longer near maximum.
lessons.lesson: Do not automatically smith at moderate HP; choose rest when the next fight can plausibly leave the run unable to recover. Preserving enough HP for the following floors is often more valuable than one additional upgrade.
evidence_points: At Floor 6, HP was 69/80 and smith was chosen instead of rest.
The next logged combat was against Gremlin Nob, and HP fell from 69/80 to 24/80 by Floor 7.
lessons.reasoning: The upgrade did not prevent a large HP loss in the following elite fight, leaving the run at 24 HP for the remainder of the route. This supports treating campfire healing as a risk-control decision rather than defaulting to upgrades.

lessons.title: Secure immediate block when low HP and attacks are incoming
lessons.situation: When HP is low, block is zero or minimal, and the visible enemies have attack intents.
lessons.lesson: Prefer immediately playable block or damage-mitigation cards over draw or setup unless the setup directly prevents the current damage. In particular, reassess draw/exhaust lines when they leave no block before an incoming attack.
evidence_points: On Turn 7 of the Slime Boss fight, HP was 21/80 and Block was 0 while both enemies showed ATTACK_DEBUFF intents.
Shrug It Off, Flame Barrier, and Second Wind were legal, but Battle Trance was played first and Second Wind was chosen afterward; the next logged state showed HP 12/80 and Block 0.
lessons.reasoning: The logged sequence shows that the turn's setup did not leave block for the incoming damage, and HP dropped by the next turn. The reusable correction is to value guaranteed immediate mitigation more highly in this exact low-HP/attack-intent state.

lessons.title: Consider removal before adding several cards to a basic deck
lessons.situation: At a shop with low HP, a still-basic-heavy deck, and enough gold for removal plus other purchases.
lessons.lesson: Evaluate card removal as a priority before buying multiple situational additions; improving draw quality can be safer than continuing to expand the deck when the run already needs consistency.
evidence_points: At the Floor 10 shop, HP was 24/80, gold was 263, and card removal for 75 gold was available.
The final 20-card deck still contained four Strikes and four Defends, while the shop purchases added Second Wind, Inflame, and Whirlwind.
lessons.reasoning: The run had both a low-HP survival problem and a deck containing all eight basic cards. Removing a weak basic card would have improved the odds of drawing the newly acquired defensive and scaling cards without increasing deck size; future shops should weigh that consistency gain before making several additions.
